title: 3.7.22 Lab: Array-Methods Capstone
description: Combine the module's non-mutating tools: build a list, transform it with .map(), take a range with .slice(), join with .concat() or spread, and copy an object with an override. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build a source list
steps.instructions: Create a variable called prices and fill it with at least five numbers, using .push() as you build.

steps.title: Transform with .map()
steps.instructions: Use .map() to build a new array where every price is increased by a fixed amount or percentage, and store it in a second variable.

steps.title: Take a range with .slice()
steps.instructions: Use .slice() to copy a part of the transformed array into a third variable.

steps.title: Join two arrays
steps.instructions: Create a second array and join it with the range using .concat() or array spread, into a fourth variable.

steps.title: Copy an object with an override
steps.instructions: Create an object with at least two properties, then build a copy with one property changed using object spread and an override. Log it alongside the original.

steps.title: Log every result
steps.instructions: Use console.log for the transformed, sliced and joined arrays and for both objects. Confirm the original prices array still holds its starting values.

requirements.title: Array built with .push()
requirements.description: Declares an array and adds to it with .push(). Help: 3.3.2 (Array Basics: Index, push, pop)
requirements.hint: Start prices as an empty array and add each value with .push, one call per value.

requirements.title: .map() used
requirements.description: Calls .map() to transform the list. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Use .map on prices with a function that increases each price, and keep the result in a second variable.

requirements.title: .slice() used
requirements.description: Calls .slice() to copy a range. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Use .slice with a start and an end index to copy part of the transformed array.

requirements.title: Arrays joined
requirements.description: Joins two arrays with .concat() or array spread. Help: 3.7.9 (Joining Lists with .concat())
requirements.hint: Join two arrays with .concat, or with both spread inside new square brackets.

requirements.title: Object spread with override
requirements.description: Builds an object copy with a property written after the spread. Help: 3.7.14 (Spreading into a New Array or Object)
requirements.hint: Copy an object with spread in braces and write the changed property after the spread.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.7.2 (Transforming a List with .map())
requirements.hint: Log the arrays, both objects, and the original prices to confirm it did not change.

requirements.title: prices holds five or more numbers and every result is printed
requirements.description: prices is an array of at least five numbers and at least six lines were printed. Help: 3.7.20 (Example: push, then map)
requirements.hint: Build prices with five or more numbers using push, then print the three arrays, both objects and the original prices.

checks.expr: Array.isArray(prices) && prices.length >= 5 && prices.every(p => typeof p === 'number') && output.filter(l => /^\s*[\[{]/.test(l)).length >= 6
checks.fail: prices should be an array of at least five numbers, and you should print the transformed, sliced and joined arrays, both objects and the original prices (six lines).
